rule: Anaesthesia history 'on this day' (v6.01). Only dates verified against the named source. Never add a date without a source. md = MM-DD.

items.x: Cuban anaesthesiologist Manuel Martínez Curbelo placed the first described continuous lumbar epidural catheter.
Harold Griffith and his resident Enid Johnson gave curare (Intocostrin) during cyclopropane anaesthesia for an appendicectomy in Montreal: the start of muscle relaxants in anaesthesia.
In Jefferson, Georgia, Crawford Long used ether to remove a small neck tumour from James Venable. He did not publish until 1849.
John Snow gave chloroform to Queen Victoria for the birth of Prince Leopold, which did much for the acceptance of pain relief in labour.
John Snow again gave chloroform to Queen Victoria, this time for the birth of Princess Beatrice.
August Bier demonstrated intravenous regional anaesthesia at the German Surgical Society congress in Berlin, with a lower-limb amputation and an elbow resection.
In Kiel, August Bier performed surgery under spinal anaesthesia with cocaine. He and his assistant Hildebrandt later tried it on each other.
William Morton extracted a tooth under ether in Boston, two weeks before the public demonstration.

William Morton anaesthetised Gilbert Abbott with ether at Massachusetts General Hospital for removal of a neck tumour: the first public demonstration of surgical anaesthesia. Now World Anaesthesia Day.
James Young Simpson and his friends Keith and Duncan inhaled chloroform after dinner in Edinburgh and woke up under the table.
James Young Simpson used chloroform in obstetrics for the first time.
The day after seeing a laughing-gas show, Hartford dentist Horace Wells had his own tooth pulled under nitrous oxide.
